knowledge_point.title: Combining Logarithms With Coefficients Using the Quotient Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's recall the quotient rule for logarithms:

$$
\log_n(a)-\log_n(b)=\log_n\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)
$$

If we factor the given expression and use the quotient rule for logarithms, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\log_{5}(198)-3\log_{5}(18)&=3\bigl(\log_{5}(198)-\log_{5}(18)\bigr) \\ &=3\log_{5}(\frac{198}{18}) \\ &=3\log_{5}(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
3\log_{5}(198)-3\log_{5}(18)=3\log_{5}(11)
$$

$$
\ln(a)-\ln(b)=\ln\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)

\begin{aligned}7\ln(18)-7\ln(2)&=7\bigl(\ln(18)-\ln(2)\bigr) \\ &=7\ln(\frac{18}{2}) \\ &=7\ln(9)\end{aligned}
